finding.claim: Missing authorization enforcement in update_doc: can_edit() result is discarded, so any authenticated user can overwrite any document's body. The sibling update_title correctly uses require_edit (line 27), confirming the intended check.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (g.user) sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON {"body": ...} for a doc_id they do not own or edit
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to document store)

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> accepts doc_id from URL
doc = DOCS[doc_id] looked up with no ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns a bool that is ignored; no abort(403)

finding.guards_checked: can_edit is called but its return value is unused; require_edit (which aborts 403) is not used here. No auth decorator or before_request hook exists in the file (g.user is assumed set elsewhere). No other checks on the path.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit() called at docs.py:19 as a bare statement, so its bool result is discarded. require_edit (docs.py:11-13), which aborts 403, is used only in update_title. No before_request hook, decorator, or other check exists in the directory.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) and discards the bool, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any user. This differs from update_title, where require_edit at docs.py:27 aborts with 403.
